sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐秘。

sentences.en: You probably have a favorite local TV ad.
sentences.zh: 你可能有一个最喜欢的本地电视广告。

sentences.en: Something that's low budget, with lots of graphics and terrible music,
sentences.zh: 那种低预算、有大量图形和糟糕音乐的广告，

sentences.en: and it stars a fun, charismatic, in-your-face local business owner,
sentences.zh: 里面由一位有趣、有魅力、咄咄逼人的本地企业老板主演，

sentences.en: like New York's favorite stereo salesman, Crazy Eddie.
sentences.zh: 比如纽约最受欢迎的音响销售员疯狂埃迪。

sentences.en: It's a Crazy Eddie Christmas in August!
sentences.zh: 八月的疯狂埃迪圣诞节！

sentences.en: Crazy Eddie's gonna save you a blizzard of bucks on stereo rack systems,
sentences.zh: 疯狂埃迪将在立体声音响组合上为你省下一大笔钱，
或者马丁家具的那位老兄。

sentences.en: Hi, Marty McDermott for the Martin Furniture Store.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是马丁家具店的马蒂·麦克德莫特。

sentences.en: We own this furniture business in Indiana, and our prices are out of this world.
sentences.zh: 我们在印第安纳州拥有这家家具店，我们的价格不可思议。

sentences.en: But if you grew up in Toronto in the 1980s,
sentences.zh: 但如果你在20世纪80年代的多伦多长大，

sentences.en: you probably know our local supermarket guy, Dave Nickel.
sentences.zh: 你可能认识我们的本地超市老兄戴夫·尼科尔。

sentences.en: By contrast, he was extremely low-key.
That's producer and notable Canadian, Chris Berupe.
sentences.zh: 那是制作人兼知名的加拿大人克里斯·贝鲁普。

sentences.en: Dave Nickel might be the most milquetoast guy to appear on television.
sentences.zh: 戴夫·尼科尔可能是电视上出现过最温顺的人了。

sentences.en: He had these big wire-framed glasses and this dome of brown hair
sentences.zh: 他戴着那种粗铁丝框架的眼镜，顶着一头圆圆的棕色头发，

sentences.en: and a prominent Southern Ontario accent.
sentences.zh: 带着浓重南安大略口音。

sentences.en: In the past few weeks, there's been a lot of shouting about lower grocery prices.
sentences.zh: 在过去几周里，有很多关于杂货降价的呐喊声。

sentences.en: Recently, the major newspapers in Toronto and Ottawa compared prices at the major supermarkets.
sentences.zh: 最近，多伦多和渥太华的主要报纸对比了各大超市的价格。

sentences.en: In both surveys, Loblaws had the lowest prices.
sentences.zh: 在这两项调查中，Loblaws超市的价格都是最低的。

sentences.en: In the 80s, Nickel helped run a grocery store chain called Loblaws, which makes me giggle just to say it.
sentences.zh: 在80年代，尼科尔曾帮助运营一家名为Loblaws的连锁超市，光是说出这个名字就让我咯咯笑。

sentences.en: They had an inexpensive line of products they called the no-name brand,
sentences.zh: 他们有一系列价格便宜的产品，被称为无品牌系列，

sentences.en: which Nickel would sell in a series of sleep-inducing commercials.
sentences.zh: 尼科尔在一系列催眠般的广告中推销这些产品。

sentences.en: For example, these brand-name pickles are almost twice as expensive as no-name.
sentences.zh: 例如，这些名牌泡菜的价格几乎是无品牌产品的两倍。

sentences.en: Why is it then that in many supermarkets you find the national brand in one hour...
sentences.zh: 那么为什么在许多超市里，你会在一个小时内找到国家品牌……

sentences.en: In these ads, Nickel would sit on a stool in front of a black background,
sentences.zh: 在这些广告中，尼科尔会坐在黑色背景前的凳子上，

sentences.en: Though sometimes for added excitement, he'd include his dog in the ad.
sentences.zh: 虽然有时为了增加兴奋感，他会把他的狗带进广告里。

sentences.en: This is Georgie Girl, and she's a French bulldog.
sentences.zh: 这是乔治女孩，她是一只法国斗牛犬。

sentences.en: These discount ads were part of a strategy.
sentences.zh: 这些折扣广告是一项策略的一部分。

sentences.en: The ads were notably plain, just like the products,
sentences.zh: 这些广告明显很朴素，就像产品一样，

sentences.en: because no-name had basically no package design.
sentences.zh: 因为无品牌系列基本上没有包装设计。

sentences.en: If you bought no-name cookies, here's what you get.
sentences.zh: 如果你买无品牌饼干，这就是你得到的。

sentences.en: A box with some cookies inside.
sentences.zh: 一个里面装了几块饼干的盒子。

sentences.en: Which, you know, I guess that's what you always get.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我想这就是你一直得到的。

sentences.en: But in this case, the box had a plain background with black text that said,
sentences.zh: 但在这个例子中，盒子的背景很朴素，上面写着黑色的文字，

sentences.en: There was no-name peanut butter, no-name detergent, no-name orange juice.
sentences.zh: 有无品牌花生酱、无品牌洗涤剂、无品牌橙汁。

sentences.en: All of it was dirt cheap.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都便宜得要命。
而且Loblaws并不是独一无二的。

sentences.en: It was one of the many supermarket chains across North America
sentences.zh: 它是北美众多连锁超市之一，

sentences.en: that was riding a generic product craze in the late 70s and the early 80s.
sentences.zh: 在70年代末和80年代初顺应了通用产品热潮。

sentences.en: But Loblaws took it further than anyone.
sentences.zh: 但Loblaws比任何人都走得更远。

sentences.en: Their generic marketing plan changed the way we eat and shop.
sentences.zh: 他们的通用营销计划改变了我们的饮食和购物方式。

sentences.en: And ironically, their strategy to go brandless
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，他们走向无品牌的策略

sentences.en: became one of the most successful branding campaigns.
sentences.zh: 成为了最成功的品牌推广活动之一。

sentences.en: About 100 years ago, we really didn't have supermarkets.
sentences.zh: 大约100年前，我们其实没有超市。

sentences.en: If you went shopping, you had to go to the green grocer and the butcher,
sentences.zh: 如果你去购物，你必须去绿色蔬菜店和肉铺，

sentences.en: and then someone delivered your milk, and it was so, so time-consuming.
sentences.zh: 然后有人给你送牛奶，这太耗时了。

sentences.en: But in 1916, Clarence Saunders opened a store in Tennessee called Piggly Wiggly,
sentences.zh: 但在1916年，克拉伦斯·桑德斯在田纳西州开了一家名为Piggly Wiggly的商店，

sentences.en: which was the first place with self-service groceries.
sentences.zh: 这是第一家提供自助式杂货的地方。

sentences.en: Rows and rows of products that you could pick out yourself.
sentences.zh: 一排又一排你可以自己挑选的产品。

sentences.en: Soon, America was overrun with grocery stores.
sentences.zh: 很快，美国到处都是杂货店。

sentences.en: After World War II, these stores were filled with famous national brands.
sentences.zh: 二战后，这些商店里充满了著名的国家品牌。

sentences.en: A couple of factors helped the big brands take over,
sentences.zh: 几个因素帮助大品牌占据了主导地位，

sentences.en: like the new interstate highway system, which made it easy to deliver goods.
sentences.zh: 比如新的州际高速公路系统，这使得运送货物变得容易。

sentences.en: And, of course, the rise of television.
When you have your weight, you start every day with a voice.
sentences.zh: 当你有了分量，你每天都从一个声音开始。

sentences.en: When the look on the face is happy, the name on the bottle must be Heinz Ketchup.
sentences.zh: 当脸上的表情是快乐的，瓶子上的名字一定亨氏番茄酱。

sentences.en: Think about the cereal aisle, soft drinks, cleaning detergents, Procter & Gamble,
sentences.zh: 想想麦片过道、软饮料、清洁剂、宝洁、

sentences.en: Those were the biggest advertisers in the post-war era.
sentences.zh: 那是战后时代最大的广告商。

sentences.en: They really are the big spenders, and the big spenders were the brands most people wanted.
sentences.zh: 他们确实是大金主，而大金主正是大多数人想要的品牌。

sentences.en: This is my favorite marketer, Terry O'Reilly.
sentences.zh: 这是我最喜欢的营销人员特里·奥赖利。

sentences.en: And I am the host of Under the Influence, which is a CBC radio show and podcast,
sentences.zh: 我是《受其影响》的主持人，这是一档CBC广播节目和播客，

sentences.en: and I am a 40-year ad man.
sentences.zh: 我是一个有40年经验的广告人。

sentences.en: O'Reilly says back at the advent of TV,
sentences.zh: 奥赖利说，在电视刚出现的时候，

sentences.en: telling people about your new product was pretty easy
sentences.zh: 向人们介绍你的新产品相当容易，

sentences.en: if you had the money to buy commercials on the biggest shows.
sentences.zh: 如果你有钱在最大的节目上买广告的话。

sentences.en: There was a time when you could buy the Ed Sullivan Show and Bonanza and maybe Gunsmoke back in the 60s,
sentences.zh: 曾几何时，在60年代你可以买下《埃德·沙利文秀》、《博南扎》和可能的《荒野大镖客》，

sentences.en: and by buying just those three programs, you would be reaching 80% of America and Canada.
sentences.zh: 只要买下这三个节目，你就能覆盖80%的美国和加拿大。
名牌产品占据了统治地位。

sentences.en: They were most of what people bought at grocery stores in North America.
sentences.zh: 它们是人们在北美杂货店里买得最多的东西。

sentences.en: To fill out the shelves, supermarkets would make their own store brand products, too.
sentences.zh: 为了填满货架，超市也会制作自己的店面品牌产品。

sentences.en: Often, these looked kind of like the big brands, with the name of the supermarket slapped on the side of the box.
sentences.zh: 通常，这些产品看起来有点像大品牌，盒子侧面印着超市的名字。

sentences.en: Store brands were mostly popular with people who wanted a low-budget alternative to the name brand stuff.
sentences.zh: 店面品牌主要受那些想要找名牌产品的低预算替代品的人欢迎。

sentences.en: They wanted to buy something that was, you know, not as good, but not as expensive.
sentences.zh: 他们想买一些你知道的、没那么好但也没那么贵的东西。

sentences.en: He's an emeritus marketing professor at the Wharton School.
sentences.zh: 他是沃顿商学院的名誉营销教授。

sentences.en: And he says store brands weren't always the highest quality,
sentences.zh: 他说店面品牌并不总是质量最高的，

sentences.en: but many of them were close enough to the name brands,
sentences.zh: 但其中许多产品与名牌非常接近，

sentences.en: mainly because a lot of grocery store products are easy to make.
sentences.zh: 主要是因为很多杂货店的产品很容易制作。

sentences.en: You need some machine that can spit out corn batter
sentences.zh: 你需要一台能把玉米面糊喷出来的机器，

sentences.en: into some machine that nukes it, and all of a sudden it's a cornflake.
sentences.zh: 放进一台用微波炉加热的机器里，突然它就成了玉米片。

sentences.en: So there's always a bunch of manufacturers that can do it.
sentences.zh: 所以总有一群制造商可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: And, you know, for instance, shampoo.
You know, anybody can make shampoo.
sentences.zh: 你知道，任何人都可以做洗发水。

sentences.en: All you need is a bathtub and some chemicals and some bottles.
sentences.zh: 你只需要一个浴缸、一些化学品和一些瓶子。

sentences.en: But the store brands weren't big sellers until they received a boost in the late 1970s.
sentences.zh: 但直到20世纪70年代末受到推动之前，店面品牌并不是大卖产品。

sentences.en: After the oil crisis, the global economy went into a recession.
sentences.zh: 石油危机之后，全球经济陷入衰退。

sentences.en: And suddenly, middle-class families didn't have money for name brands like Coke or Kellogg's.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，中产阶级家庭没有钱买可口可乐或家乐氏这样的名牌了。
消费者想要更便宜的食物。

sentences.en: In response, there was a new demand for low-cost store brands.
sentences.zh: 作为回应，对低成本店面品牌有了新的需求。

sentences.en: One chain in France called Carrefour was developing one of these discount brands
sentences.zh: 法国的一家名为家乐福的连锁店正在开发这些折扣品牌之一，
当时他们有了这个想法。

sentences.en: Instead of using bright colors or putting their name on the box
sentences.zh: 不用鲜艳的颜色，不用把他们的名字印在盒子上，

sentences.en: or using slogans, you know, branding,
sentences.zh: 也不用口号，你知道的，搞品牌宣传，
他们的产品将是没有品牌的。

sentences.en: Just the name of the food in black text on a white background.
sentences.zh: 只有白色背景上黑字写着的食物名称。

sentences.en: This minimalist design was a brilliant marketing tool.
sentences.zh: 这种极简主义设计是一个极好的营销工具。

sentences.en: It delivered the message that this is cheap.
sentences.zh: 它传达了一个信息：这是便宜的。

sentences.en: We're cutting costs and we are passing the savings down to you.
sentences.zh: 我们正在削减成本，并将节省下来的钱转让给你。

sentences.en: This is bare bones and you're having a hard time coping here
sentences.zh: 这是最基础的，你在这里很难应付，

sentences.en: because, you know, maybe you're unemployed or whatever.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，也许你失业了或者别的什么。

sentences.en: And so here's a way that you can substitute away from a more expensive product
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一种方法，你可以从更昂贵的产品中替代出来，

sentences.en: and still satisfy your kids when they wake up in the morning
sentences.zh: 同时还能满足你的孩子们，当他们早上醒来时，

sentences.en: and they want some cereal for breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 他们想吃点麦片作为早餐。

sentences.en: In 1976, Carrefour launched the new product line,
sentences.zh: 1976年，家乐福推出了新的产品线，

sentences.en: which they called Les Produits Libra,
which means in English, free products,
sentences.zh: 用英语来说就是免费产品，

sentences.en: which, you know, they weren't actually free.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它们实际上并不是免费的。

sentences.en: But these products were 20-30% cheaper than everything else at the store.
sentences.zh: 但这些产品比店里的其他东西便宜20-30%。

sentences.en: Soon, the Broadway Libra were a hit.
sentences.zh: 不久，“自由产品”大获成功。

sentences.en: Virtue store executives from North America
were actually flying to Europe just to check out Carrefour
sentences.zh: 实际上飞往欧洲只是为了看看家乐福，

sentences.en: and see what the hype was about.
sentences.zh: 看看这股狂热是怎么回事。

sentences.en: Soon, the Broadway Libra idea was being copied by everybody.
sentences.zh: 很快，“自由产品”的理念就被所有人效仿了。

sentences.en: Stephen Hoke says, at first, it was a bit of a shock.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬·霍克说，起初，这有点令人震惊。

sentences.en: I just had moved to Chicago
and the big grocery chain there was called Jewel.
sentences.zh: 那里的主要连锁超市叫朱尔。

sentences.en: I remember going to the store
and all of a sudden, I saw these black and white packages.
sentences.zh: 突然间，我看到了这些黑白包装。

sentences.en: It was black type on a white package
for every single one of those things.
sentences.zh: 白色包装上的黑色字体。

sentences.en: You know, so it said napkins.
sentences.zh: 你知道，上面写着餐巾纸。
这就像极简主义者的天堂。

sentences.en: Chain stores like Jewel in Chicago and Ralph's in California
sentences.zh: 像芝加哥的朱尔和加利福尼亚的拉尔夫这样的连锁店

sentences.en: were packaging and selling their own generic products.
sentences.zh: 都在包装和销售他们自己的通用产品。

sentences.en: In many stores, the generic products were given a separate aisle.
sentences.zh: 在许多商店里，通用产品被分配到一个单独的过道。
这有助于推广它们的新颖性。

sentences.en: But it also prevented shoppers from comparing them side by side
sentences.zh: 但这也可以防止购物者将它们与看起来更好的名牌产品进行并排比较。

sentences.en: with the nicer looking brand name products.
sentences.zh: 但这可以防止购物者将它们与外观更好的名牌产品并排比较。
但有一家加拿大杂货店

sentences.en: took this idea of generic branding to a whole new extreme.
sentences.zh: 将通用品牌的这个概念推向了一个全新的极端。

sentences.en: And the catalyst was the man a lot of Canadians knew from local TV ads.
sentences.zh: 而催化剂是许多加拿大人从本地电视广告中认识的那个人。

sentences.en: The president of Loblaw's supermarkets, Dave Nichol.
sentences.zh: Loblaws超市的总裁戴夫·尼科尔。

sentences.en: Dave Nichol wasn't born rich, but he was a man of refined tastes.
sentences.zh: 戴夫·尼科尔并非出生富贵，但他是一个有着精细品味的人。

sentences.en: He went to Harvard Law School.
sentences.zh: 他曾就读于哈佛法学院。

sentences.en: He loved to fly first class.
And he personally knew the chefs at many of the three-star restaurants in Europe.
sentences.zh: 而且他个人认识欧洲许多三星级餐厅的主厨。

sentences.en: Dave Nichol was friends with Galen Weston,
sentences.zh: 戴夫·尼科尔和盖伦·韦斯顿是朋友，

sentences.en: who was from one of the richest families in Canada.
sentences.zh: 韦斯顿家族是加拿大最富有的家族之一。

sentences.en: The Westons owned Loblaw's, and they tapped Dave Nichol to help run the company,
sentences.zh: 韦斯顿家族拥有洛布劳公司，他们委任戴夫·尼科尔来协助运营这家公司，

sentences.en: even though he had no experience running a supermarket.
sentences.zh: 尽管他没有任何运营超市的经验。

sentences.en: At the time, Loblaw's was in a really bad place.
sentences.zh: 当时，洛布劳公司的处境非常糟糕。

sentences.en: They were trailing way behind their competitor, the grocery chain Dominion.
sentences.zh: 他们远远落后于竞争对手——杂货连锁店多米宁。

sentences.en: Loblaw's was closing stores and laying off workers.
sentences.zh: 洛布劳当时在不断关闭门店并裁员。

sentences.en: The only thing Loblaw's had going for it was a celebrity pitchman named William Shatner.
sentences.zh: 洛布劳唯一拿得出手的东西是一位名叫威廉·夏特纳的名人代言人。

sentences.en: Hey, right now, Loblaw's is having a huge frozen food sale.
sentences.zh: 嘿，现在洛布劳正在举行盛大的冷冻食品大促销。

sentences.en: Frozen vegetables, frozen meat entrees, frozen concentrated juices, ice cream.
sentences.zh: 冷冻蔬菜、冷冻肉类主菜、冷冻浓缩果汁、冰淇淋。

sentences.en: If it's frozen, you can save plenty.
sentences.zh: 只要是冷冻的，你就能省下一大笔钱。

sentences.en: Don't get left out on the cold.
Nichol saw the low sales and the stores closing,
sentences.zh: 尼科尔看到销量惨淡和门店纷纷倒闭，

sentences.en: and he decided, we need to change things up.
sentences.zh: 他决定，我们需要做出改变。

sentences.en: So Loblaw's took Carefor's discount branding idea,
sentences.zh: 于是洛布劳借鉴了家乐福的折扣品牌理念，

sentences.en: It was just like the black and white generics you could find in America and Europe.
sentences.zh: 它就像你在美国和欧洲能看到的黑白无牌商品一样。

sentences.en: But the Loblaw's products had one big design flourish.
sentences.zh: 但洛布劳的产品有一个很大的设计亮点。

sentences.en: We hired a great designer named Don Watt,
sentences.zh: 我们雇了一位伟大的设计师叫唐·瓦特，

sentences.en: who just chose yellow, stark banana yellow,
sentences.zh: 他选中了黄色，刺眼的香蕉黄，

sentences.en: and just big, chunky Helvetica type.
sentences.zh: 以及巨大的、厚重的黑体字。

sentences.en: Yellow feels like a discount color, I guess like its cousin orange.
sentences.zh: 黄色感觉像是一种折扣的颜色，我想就像它的表亲橙色一样。

sentences.en: And I think Don Watt really chose yellow
sentences.zh: 而且我认为唐·瓦特选择黄色真的是因为

sentences.en: because it was a color least used by big brands.
sentences.zh: 这是大品牌最少使用的颜色。

sentences.en: It was almost like Orwellian, no romance in it.
sentences.zh: 它几乎带有一种奥威尔式的风格，里面没有一丝浪漫。

sentences.en: But Nichol didn't just launch the product line.
sentences.zh: 但尼科尔不仅推出了这条产品线。

sentences.en: He made it an entire store.
